spatial_claims.claim: Lines l and m are parallel; l is perpendicular to plane Pi at point O; they lie in plane Sigma different from Pi; Sigma intersects Pi in line s through O
Line m meets line s at point B, with B different from O; B lies in Pi on s
l is perpendicular to s at O (since l perp Pi and s in Pi); m is perpendicular to s at B (by 1.29 on transversal s cutting parallels l,m)
BE drawn in Pi at right angles to s at B; E in Pi, E not on s; A on l with A different from O (A not in Pi); OE lies in Pi; AB lies in Sigma
Angle AOE is right (l perp Pi, OE in Pi); angle AOB is right (l perp Pi, OB along s in Pi); angle OBE is right (BE perp s at B)
Pythagorean theorem on triangles AOE, OBE, AOB giving AE^2=AO^2+OE^2, OE^2=OB^2+BE^2, AB^2=AO^2+OB^2
AE^2 = AB^2 + BE^2 by algebraic substitution; angle ABE is right by converse Pythagorean theorem 1.48
BE perpendicular to both BA and BO at B; BA and BO are distinct intersecting lines in Sigma; by 11.4 BE is perpendicular to Sigma; hence BE perpendicular to m
m perpendicular to both BO (part of s) and BE at B; BO and BE are distinct intersecting lines in Pi; by 11.4 m is perpendicular to Pi

configuration_map: O: lies in Pi, on line l, on line s (= Sigma intersect Pi). B: lies in Pi, on line m, on line s, B != O. A: on line l, A != O, hence NOT in Pi (since l perp Pi at O). E: in Pi, BE perp s at B, hence E not on s and E != O. Line s: lies in both Sigma and Pi, passes through O and B. Line l: lies in Sigma, perpendicular to Pi at O. Line m: lies in Sigma, parallel to l, meets Pi at B. Plane Sigma: contains l, m, s, AB. Plane Pi: contains s, OE, BE, B, O, E. Throughout the proof, A remains above Pi, E remains in Pi off of s, and all plane memberships are consistently maintained. The three right triangles (AOE, OBE, AOB) are well-formed with verified right angles at the correct vertices.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The proof uses a different method from Heath (Pythagorean theorem 1.47 and its converse 1.48 instead of congruent triangles) but the geometric configuration is sound. Key verifications: (1) all three Pythagorean theorem applications have valid right angles at the correct vertices, (2) the algebraic combination correctly yields angle ABE = 90 degrees, (3) both applications of 11.4 have the required distinct intersecting lines in the correct planes with the perpendicular line not lying in those planes, (4) all point positions (A above Pi, E in Pi off s, O and B on s) are maintained consistently throughout.
